subject: Hidden Markov Model with two outputs: How to define the hidden categorical parameter z?

messages.author: 8c3e0c4226a5e3e2
messages.subject: Hidden Markov Model with two outputs: How to define the hidden categorical parameter z?
parts:
Hello Folks,
I am trying to fit a standard HMM in Stan (in an unsupervised way) with two different output variables from the hidden state, z, including (i) the observations, y, and (ii) the segmentation variable (Seg). The latter is sampled from a Bernoulli to indicate whether hidden state, z, is stable or not. So two questions:
  1. How can I define a hidden state z as a parameter in Stan considering that its Categorical? After an exhausting search within the mailing list, I saw some responses suggesting to define z as real in the parameters-block, then converting it to discrete in the model-block. I did that in my code below.
  2. How can I resolve the following error that I get when I run the code? (Test dataset is attached)
[1] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                        
[2] "Exception thrown at line 41: beta_log: Random variable[3] is 7.3254, but must be less than or equal to 1"                              
[3] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
[4] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."                              
[5] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                              
[6] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."

Here is the Stan code:

```{r}
my_model <- "
functions {
    // Define transformation function
  int int_floor(real x) {
    int i;
    i = 0;
    if (x >= 0) while (x > i + 1) i = i + 1;
    else while (x < i) i = i - 1;
    return i;
  }
}
data {
  int<lower=1> S; // num hidden states
  int<lower=0> T; // num timesteps
  int<lower=0> N; // num obs
  real<lower=0> y[N, T]; // obs
}
parameters {
  real<lower=1,upper=S> z; // hidden states
  real<lower=0,upper=1> Seg; // segmentation var 
  vector<lower=0>[S] mu_y; // emit probs
  vector<lower=0>[S] sigma_y; // emit probs
  simplex[S] pi[S]; // transit probs
  vector<lower=0>[S] omega; // prior on Seg
  vector<lower=0>[S] beta; // prior on pi
}
model {
  // Define the discrete variables
  int z_int[T];
  int Seg_int[T];

  // Transform continuous latent state to integer
  for (t in 1:T)
    z_int[t] = int_floor(z);

  // Transform continuous segmentation to integer
  for (t in 1:T)
    Seg_int[t] = int_floor(Seg);

  // uniform prior on omega
  omega ~ beta(1, 1);
 
  // likelihood of the segmentation variable
  for (t in 1:T)
    Seg_int[t] ~ bernoulli(omega[z_int[t]]);
  
  // uniform prior on beta
  beta ~ uniform(0, 1); 

  // the likelihood of transition
  for (s in 1:S)
    pi[s] ~ dirichlet(beta);

  // the likelihood of the hidden states
  for (t in 2:T)
    z_int[t] ~ categorical(pi[z_int[t - 1]]);

  // prior on mean of observations
  for (s in 1:S)
    mu_y[s] ~ normal(0, 10); 

  // prior on std deviation of observations
  for (s in 1:S)
    sigma_y[s] ~ inv_gamma(1, 10);

  // likelihood of the observations
  for (t in 1:T) 
    y[t] ~ normal(mu_y[z_int[t]], sigma_y[z_int[t]]);
}
"
```

Sampling code
```{r}
obs <- readRDS("~/data/obs_test.rds")
my_data <- list(S = ncol(obs), T = ncol(obs), N = nrow(obs), y = obs)
my_fit <- stan(model_code = my_model, data = my_data, chains = 5, iter = 6000)
```

Thanks,
-- Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Hidden Markov Model with two outputs: How to define the hidden categorical parameter z?
parts:
On Monday, December 5, 2016 at 9:02:26 PM UTC-5, Daniel Emaasit wrote:
  1. How can I define a hidden state z as a parameter in Stan considering that its Categorical? After an exhausting search within the mailing list, I saw some responses suggesting to define z as real in the parameters-block, then converting it to discrete in the model-block. I did that in my code below.

That doesn't work well because it mess up the gradient information in the original variable, which is essential for Hamiltonian Monte Carlo. You have to marginalize out the discrete categorical variables.

1. How can I resolve the following error that I get when I run the code? (Test dataset is attached)
[1] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                        
[2] "Exception thrown at line 41: beta_log: Random variable[3] is 7.3254, but must be less than or equal to 1"                              
[3] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
[4] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."                              
[5] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                              
[6] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."

Declare omega with an upper bound of 1, as in

vector<lower=0,upper=1>[S] omega;

Ben

define its density. There's an example in the manual and
we've been discussing movement HMMs on the users list
